scope: Focused primary-material acquisition; two consumed neutron-Compton primaries plus one consumed pure-PdH INS exclusion; no broad campaign
summary: No source-backed deuteron100/300/1000eV tail established. ZrH proton data are Gaussian-compatible; PdAg proton DINS width was constrained to IINS. PurePdH anharmonic INS is not momentum-tail evidence.

citations.title: Vibrational modes and quantum zero-point energy of hydrogen in ZrH0.0155 and ZrH2
Proton Dynamics in Palladium-Silver: An Inelastic Neutron Scattering Investigation
Strong anisotropy in the inelastic neutron scattering from PdH at high energy transfer

findings.claim: Neutron Compton scattering of protons (1H nuclei), not deuterons, was measured in epsilon-ZrH2 and nominal ZrH0.0155 (hydrogen-loaded Zircaloy-2). At 6 K the dilute-composition sample is predominantly alpha-Zr plus delta-ZrH1.6 precipitates; at 550 and 617 K alpha/delta coexist. The paper estimates 23% and 59% of H in alpha solid solution at those higher temperatures. ZrH2 results reported here are at 6 K.
findings.limitations: Not ZrD2 or ZrD0.0155. Trace alloy solutes are described on p.3; do not silently relabel the Zircaloy material pure Zr.

findings.claim: The paper uses k=p/hbar, in inverse angstrom. Isotropic n(k) is a 3D momentum-space density, normalized with d^3k; J_IA(Y)=2*pi*integral_|Y|^infinity k*n(k) dk is its 1D projection. Y=m*(E-hbar^2*Q^2/(2*m))/(hbar^2*Q). J(Y,Q)=(hbar^2*Q/m)*S(Q,E). The second moment obeys integral Y^2*J dY=2*m*<K>/(3*hbar^2). The Gaussian model is n(k)=(2*pi*sigma^2)^(-3/2)*exp(-k^2/(2*sigma^2)), yielding J_IA=(2*pi*sigma^2)^(-1/2)*exp(-Y^2/(2*sigma^2)).
findings.limitations: Experimental spectra are in arbitrary intensity units (p.4); the normalized mathematical definition does not mean absolute tail populations were measured.

findings.claim: Incident neutron energy for recoil measurements was 6.2 eV. Sixteen Q groups spanning 25.0-40.0 inverse angstrom were jointly fit with resolution convolution; Fig.6 example is Q=28 inverse angstrom, 6 K. The displayed Y axis is -30 to +30 inverse angstrom, with visible data extending approximately -30 to +25 (less on the negative side for the dilute sample); this is a plot range, not a validated 3D radial cutoff. Proton recoil FWHM is approximately 10 inverse angstrom. Zr recoil near Y=-15 and fast-neutron background are explicitly modeled. Resolution FWHM falls from 3.93 to 1.54 inverse angstrom across Q=25 to40.
findings.limitations: Q is neutron momentum transfer, not initial target momentum k. The fast-neutron high-energy background is not evidence for a high-momentum hydrogen population; negative-Y Zr peak is not hydrogen non-Gaussianity.

findings.locator: p.7 Sec5.2 and Table1; p.8 conclusions
findings.claim: Reported mean proton kinetic energies (meV): ZrH2 at6K 109.0 +/-0.3; nominal ZrH0.0155 at6K112.9 +/-1.4,550K119.4 +/-1.4,617K118.3 +/-1.4. Errors are one standard deviation unless stated otherwise. Authors find a Gaussian fits at all measured temperatures and no statistical justification for a non-Gaussian n(k).
findings.limitations: Gaussian adequacy on this finite-range experiment is not a proof of an exactly Gaussian distribution at arbitrarily high k. Earlier Evans values in the table are cited historical data, not newly consumed independent measurements.

findings.claim: Anharmonicity is observed in vibrational overtones; the potential is discussed as approximately harmonic below about300meV and anharmonic above. Nevertheless the authors conclude occupied low-temperature momentum distributions are adequately Gaussian because ground and first excited states dominate.
findings.limitations: Anharmonic excited levels are not a demonstrated populated 100/300/1000eV kinetic-energy tail. A 300meV potential-energy scale is not 300eV.

findings.claim: VESUVIO DINS was actually performed on hydrogen in Pd0.77Ag0.23 membranes, not pure PdH and not PdD. Fig7 shows proton J(y_H), described as proportional to the one-dimensional momentum distribution, for300K/2bar and453K/1bar. Plotted y_H range is -20 to+20 inverse angstrom. Strong Pd/Ag prompt-gamma background impaired the measurement. Empty membrane spectra were subtracted; multiple scattering and FCT background corrections were neglected. Gaussian widths/kinetic energies were fixed to IINS predictions; only peak intensity was freely fit. Authors explicitly state they had to fix kinetic energy.
findings.limitations: Not an independent empirical n(k) shape determination or a measurement of non-Gaussian tails. No explicit 3D n(k) inversion or numerical DINS Q coverage is supplied in the consumed DINS sections. Plot range is not a sensitivity limit.

findings.locator: p.11 Table1; p.14 Table3; pp.15-16 Sec4.3
findings.claim: IINS Table3 gives <K>_H=72.1 +/-0.9meV at453K/1bar; Table1 assigns H/M=0.092 for that IINS condition from literature thermodynamics. Table3 includes333K/2bar <K>=60.6 +/-0.6meV, but no300K entry. Zero-point IINS estimate at1bar is48.3 +/-0.2meV (p.14).
findings.limitations: These are IINS-derived quantities, not freely measured DINS widths. Do not assign the333K value as an exact300K DINS measurement. Absolute H/M for300K/2bar is not specified in the DINS sections consumed; only relative intensity/uptake is reported. The 453K composition is a literature-based thermodynamic estimate, not direct stoichiometric assay.

findings.claim: Actual pure-palladium primary: stoichiometric PdH0.99 +/-0.03, protons, powder and textured plates,25K; incoherent INS over2-800meV. It reports orientation-dependent anharmonic higher vibrational levels (e.g.253,364,475meV peaks along approximately[100]) while low-energy one-phonon spectra are nearly isotropic.
findings.limitations: This is NOT a DINS/Compton measurement of n(p). No measured momentum-distribution range, J(y), mean kinetic energy or non-Gaussian n(p) tail is reported. It cannot fill the pure-PdH/PdD DINS gap or establish a large ground-state tail.

findings.claim: Exact edition sought: A.C.Evans,D.N.Timms,J.Mayers,S.M.Bennington, Neutron-scattering study of the impulse approximation in ZrH2, PhysRevB53 (1996)3023-3031, DOI10.1103/PhysRevB.53.3023. DOI route exposed abstract and authorization-required fulltext. Direct PDF request returned HTML rather than a PDF; response bytes preserved. Exact-title author/archive search returned bibliographic/DOI routes, no usable manuscript.
findings.limitations: No fulltext-dependent values or unseen sections reconstructed. Consumed publisher abstract says finite-Q asymmetry/centroid shifts diminish toward IA and can be removed by symmetrization at highQ; this is final-state/IA physics, not by itself a non-Gaussian initial-state tail. No low-p deviation is imported from an unseen edition.

findings.claim: Using nuclear masses mp=1.67262192595e-27kg and md=3.3435837768e-27kg, exact h=6.62607015e-34Js and e=1.602176634e-19C, K_D(eV)=0.001038005664243405*k^2 for k in inverse angstrom. Deuteron100/300/1000eV thresholds correspond to k=310.38458075725646/537.6018637575335/981.5222257894003 inverse angstrom. Proton thresholds are219.52951927968576/380.23628115358713/694.2132945656538 inverse angstrom.
findings.limitations: These conversions use actual isotope masses and no isotope scaling of measured distributions. J(y) samples one component; its finite displayed y window is not a hard limit on transverse momentum or a rigorous integrated radial-tail bound. No tail weights extrapolated.

findings.claim: No consumed primary demonstrates a deuteron high-momentum tail at100,300 or1000eV kinetic energy, or supplies its integrated weight. No verified measured low-p non-Gaussian deviation in these consumed papers establishes such a tail. Prisk offers a genuinely measured proton Gaussian-compatible profile; PdAg DINS is shape-constrained and Ross purePdH measures transitions, not momentum distributions.
findings.limitations: This focused acquisition does not prove the absence of all such measurements in the literature. PurePdH/PdD DINS and PdD/ZrD tail distributions remain explicit source gaps. The real bound-target calculation must stand on its own; these proton data cannot be relabeled as deuteron observations.

findings.claim: A bound-state momentum component and its kinetic-operator value do not automatically constitute an on-shell free hot-deuteron population. Free-target inverse-tail diagnostics are not unqualified bound-state fusion predictions or rigorous bounds.
findings.limitations: No simulation, reaction yield computation, fitting of S(E), site-profile optimization, repository edit or TDDFT/SCF work performed in this slice.

conversion.interpretation: Conversions only, no distribution extrapolation; y is one component and is not a 3D momentum-radius cutoff.
